answer: Delay-weighted attention ledger. Each identity accrues credit only by responding to randomly routed verification tasks after a random delay, forcing sustained monitoring rather than bulk registration. An attacker's cost is idle attention capacity: N identities demand N parallel watchers, since a single watcher leaves a hollow response pattern detectable via timing gaps. Credit accrues slowly like basalt forming, and burst-registered identities show a flat dune of activity with no depth.
